scenes.text: Hello little explorers! I'm Mino, your friendly space adventurer. Today, we're going on an exciting journey through the stars to learn about something called ADHD. Have you ever heard of it? Don't worry if you haven't, because we're going to learn all about it together. Are you ready to blast off into a world of fun and discovery? Let's get started and see what amazing things we can find out!

ADHD stands for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder. That's a big name, isn't it? But don't worry, it just means that some kids have a lot of energy and find it tricky to focus on one thing at a time. Imagine if you had a rocket engine inside you, making you want to zoom around all the time! Some kids with ADHD might feel like they're always on the go, go, go. But guess what? That's okay because everyone is unique and special in their own way!

Now, let's talk about focus. Focus is like using a telescope to look at one star in the sky. Sometimes, kids with ADHD find it hard to use their 'focus telescope' because there are so many bright stars to look at all at once. But don't worry! Just like astronauts practice to become better at using their equipment, kids can practice focusing too. It's like a fun game where you try to concentrate on one thing at a time. Would you like to try it with me?

Let's play a little game to practice focusing! Imagine we're on a spaceship and we need to count all the stars outside. Can you count to five with me? One, two, three, four, five! Great job! See, focusing can be fun and exciting. Just like counting stars, you can focus on one thing at a time, and soon you'll be a focus expert. Keep practicing, and you'll get better and better every day!

Next, let's talk about something called hyperactivity. It's a big word, but it just means having lots and lots of energy, like a rocket ready to launch. Kids with ADHD sometimes feel like they have extra energy that makes them want to move and play all the time. Imagine if you had springs in your shoes that made you bounce everywhere! While it can be fun, it can also make it hard to sit still. But there are ways to use that energy in fun and helpful ways!

Let's think about how we can use our extra energy in fun ways. Maybe you can pretend you're an astronaut on a mission, running and jumping around to explore new planets. Or you could dance like you're floating in space! Moving around can be a great way to use energy and have fun at the same time. Remember, it's okay to have lots of energy, just like a rocket ready to take off!

Would you like to try a fun dance with me? Let's pretend we're astronauts bouncing on the moon. Ready? Jump up and down, spin around, and wave your arms like you're flying in space. Wow, you're doing amazing! See how much fun it is to use your energy in a playful way? Keep moving and exploring, and you'll discover all sorts of new things you can do with your energy!

Now let's talk about routines. Routines are like a map that help us know what to do each day. They can be very helpful, especially for kids with ADHD. Imagine if you were on a space mission and had to follow a schedule to know when to eat, sleep, and explore planets. Having a routine can make you feel more organized and ready for adventure. It's like having a plan to make sure you have time for everything!

Let's think about a simple routine you can try. Maybe every morning, you can brush your teeth, get dressed, and have breakfast before starting your day. It's like preparing for a space mission, making sure everything is ready before you blast off! Following a routine can help you feel calm and ready for whatever the day brings. Would you like to try creating your own daily routine?

What would you include in your daily routine? Would you have time for playing, learning, and resting? Think about all the things you do each day and how you can fit them into your routine. Remember, a routine is like a guide to help you feel ready for the day. It's your own special schedule, just like an astronaut's mission plan!

Remember when we talked about focusing earlier? Well, routines can help with that too! When you know what comes next, it's easier to concentrate on each task. Just like following a map to find hidden treasure, routines guide you through the day. And the best part? You can change your routine as you grow and discover new interests. It's like adding new planets to explore on your space map!

Let's practice a calming routine together. We'll take three deep breaths, just like we're floating in space. Ready? Breathe in deeply, and out slowly. Again, in and out. One more time, in and out. Great job! This simple routine can help you feel calm whenever you need it. Remember, it's okay to take a moment to breathe and relax, just like astronauts do in space!

You're doing wonderfully! Remember, every time you practice focusing, using your energy, or following your routine, you're becoming a little more like an astronaut on an adventure. You have your own special way of doing things, and that's what makes you unique and amazing. Keep exploring, learning, and having fun, because you're doing a fantastic job!

Our space adventure is coming to an end, but there's so much more to discover. Remember, ADHD is just one part of who you are, and it makes you special and full of wonder. Keep practicing your focusing, using your energy, and following your routine. You're a superstar! Until next time, keep reaching for the stars, and I'll see you on our next adventure. Goodbye, little explorers!
